### Known gaps

- "Commands: StartCommandExecution (iot-jobs-data, POST /command-executions) validates the command/target ARNs, deprecation, timeout (1..43200s, default 10), parameter types and valueConditions, replays a ClientToken and 409s a different request; it publishes to $aws/commands/{things|clients}/<id>/executions/<exec>/request[/json|/cbor] and device responses on .../response[/json] move the execution (IN_PROGRESS/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/REJECTED/TIMED_OUT, cloud TIMED_OUT stays non-terminal, StartedAt/CompletedAt/StatusReason/Result) and answer on response/accepted|rejected. Open: CBOR response payloads and CBOR payload-template output are rejected (no CBOR codec dependency); the rejected error code for a malformed result/statusReason (InvalidRequest) and DeleteCommandExecution on a non-terminal execution (ConflictException) are not stated in the docs; GetCommandExecution.TimeToLive is not set; binary parameters are substituted as raw bytes.",
- ClientRequestToken idempotency is not honored for CreateCustomMetric/CreateDimension: the pinned SDK docs contradict each other (CreateCustomMetric: a different token on an existing name errors; CreateDimension: the same token errors) and name no exception type, so any replay semantics would be invented. CreateAuditSuppression/StartAuditMitigationActionsTask/StartDetectMitigationActionsTask now reject a reused token (2026-10-04).
- Rule SQL engine gaps (transform() modes, get_secret caching and MQTT3.1.1 Undefined user properties were checked against the SQL reference and are correct, not gaps): decode(...,'proto') emits field names as declared in the .proto (protojson UseProtoNames) and reads the descriptor from S3 without role authorization (the SQL reference documents neither); principal() is always Undefined (the broker has no TLS or SigV4 identity; the SQL reference gives cert thumbprint / IAM userId); Int/Int division returns a Decimal when inexact while the operator table says Int (unverifiable which the service does); unaliased non-field SELECT items and a bare @variable are keyed by their source text (key naming is not documented).
- ClientToken replay is honoured for CreatePackage, CreatePackageVersion and CreateCertificateProvider (a token held by another resource is a ConflictException, an assumption); UpdatePackage, DeletePackage, UpdatePackageVersion, DeletePackageVersion, UpdatePackageConfiguration and DisassociateSbomFromPackageVersion replay as a no-op success via a 4096-entry cache that is persisted in the snapshot (AssociateSbomWithPackageVersion is already idempotent).
- DescribeJob.BeforeSubstitution and GetJobDocument.BeforeSubstitution have no effect: documents are stored verbatim; the SDK and API reference only say 'before and after the substitution parameters have been resolved' and define neither the grammar nor the resolved value (a presigned URL signed with the job role), so any substitution would be invented.
- GetV2LoggingOptions.Verbose has no effect: the SDK output has no event-type list and no enum of logging event types exists, so any list would be invented.
- Assumptions the SDK and API reference (checked ListThingGroups, ListTopicRules) do not state: ListThingGroups.Recursive defaults to false when parentGroup is set, and ListTopicRules.Topic matches the rule topic pattern exactly. RegisterCertificate verifies the device certificate signature against CaCertificatePem when both are real X.509 PEMs (CertificateValidationException), and links the CA by PEM equality.
- Jobs MQTT: get, start-next, {jobId}/get and {jobId}/update answer on accepted/rejected and notify/notify-next are published when executions change (broker_jobs.go, broker_jobs_test.go). stepTimeoutInMinutes (1..10080, -1 cancels on UpdateJobExecution; capped by the job's timeoutConfig.inProgressTimeoutInMinutes) and that in-progress timer move an IN_PROGRESS execution to TIMED_OUT lazily on the next read/update (approximateSecondsBeforeTimedOut is reported on device and control-plane describes; no $aws/events/jobExecution/*/timed_out event). Not modelled: notification de-duplication and JobExecutionsRetryConfig retries. With --iot-mqtt-auth / IOT_MQTT_AUTH (default off, open broker) the MQTT port speaks TLS (ephemeral self-signed server certificate) and requires a client certificate registered and ACTIVE in the backend; CONNECT (client ARN), PUBLISH, RECEIVE (topic ARN) and SUBSCRIBE (topicfilter ARN) are evaluated against the policies attached to the certificate ARN, with Allow/Deny, wildcards and ${iot:ClientId} / ${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName} (thing named as the client ID with the certificate attached); a denied CONNECT is refused, a denied PUBLISH is dropped (v3.1.1 QoS 1 disconnects), a denied SUBSCRIBE gets suback 0x80 (broker_auth.go). Policies attached to a thing group (and its ancestor groups) also apply when the certificate is attached to the thing named by the client ID; certificates outside NotBefore/NotAfter are refused at the handshake; policies are evaluated by iam.EvaluatePolicies, so Condition blocks work over ${iot:Connection.Thing.Attributes[attr]}, ThingTypeName, IsAttached and ${iot:Certificate.Subject.CommonName}. Certificate policy variables (broker_auth_cert.go): iot:Certificate.Subject.* / Issuer.* attributes (DistinguishedNameQualifier, Country, Organization, OrganizationalUnit, State, CommonName, SerialNumber, Title, Surname, GivenName, Initials, Pseudonym, GenerationQualifier) with the first value by default, .N for later values and .List (comma-joined, usable with ForAnyValue), iot:Certificate.SerialNumber in decimal, and Subject/Issuer AlternativeName DNSName, RFC822Name, UniformResourceIdentifier, IPAddress; a value with a wildcard character (* $ + ? #) or over 1024 bytes is left unsubstituted and at most five values are read, per the docs. Custom authorizers (broker_custom_auth.go, authorizer_invoke.go): with --iot-mqtt-auth a client without a certificate authenticates through the authorizer named by the x-amz-customauthorizer-name username query parameter or the default authorizer; the username query carries the token (the authorizer's tokenKeyName) and x-amz-customauthorizer-signature (RSA SHA-256 over the token, checked against tokenSigningPublicKeys unless signing is disabled; an unverified signature is refused without invoking the function). The authorizer's Lambda is invoked in-process with token, signatureVerified, protocols, protocolData.tls/mqtt and connectionMetadata.id; the answer is validated (principalId [a-zA-Z0-9]{1,128}, at most 10 policyDocuments of 2048 characters, disconnectAfterInSeconds/refreshAfterInSeconds 300..86400, disconnect default 86400) and its policies authorise CONNECT/PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE/RECEIVE (${iot:ClientId} works); the policies are cached for refreshAfterInSeconds and re-fetched lazily on the next authorisation, and the connection is closed after disconnectAfterInSeconds (injectable BrokerClock). TestInvokeAuthorizer forwards httpContext, tlsContext and mqttContext to the Lambda and answers InvalidResponseException for a malformed answer and ServiceUnavailableException when no Lambda service is wired. Assumptions the docs leave open: the event's mqtt.username is the full username including the query string; refreshAfterInSeconds is 0 (no refresh) when the function omits it; HTTP-protocol authorizers (iotdata Publish with x-amz-customauthorizer-*) are not wired. Not modelled with auth: AlternativeName.DirectoryName, iot:Certificate.AvailableKeys and CertificateId (format not documented), iot:Connection.Thing.ThingGroupNames (no variable of that name in the policy-variable docs; group policies still apply via the group ARNs). WebSocket auth is not modelled. The MQTT port is --iot-mqtt-port / IOT_MQTT_PORT (default 1883, 0 picks a free port); DescribeEndpoint returns a host only, as the real API does.
- Policy documents must be JSON with a string Version and Statement object/array whose entries have Effect Allow|Deny, Action|NotAction and Resource|NotResource (MalformedPolicyException otherwise, CreatePolicy and CreatePolicyVersion); an empty Statement array, Condition contents and action/resource name validity are not checked.
- $aws/events not covered: POLICY (the SDK enum has it, the developer guide documents no topic) and CA_CERTIFICATE (`$aws/events/certificates/registered/<caCertificateId>` fires on just-in-time registration, which the broker does not do: a client certificate must already be registered and ACTIVE). Lifecycle events omit `thingName` (exclusive-thing connections are not modeled) and never reset `versionNumber` after an hour offline; AUTH_ERROR, FORBIDDEN_ACCESS, SERVER_ERROR, THROTTLED, WEBSOCKET_TTL_EXPIRATION and CUSTOMAUTH_TTL_EXPIRATION disconnect reasons are not produced (no such causes exist or they are not tracked by the broker); connect_failed is published only for failures after the TLS handshake (custom authorizer or policy), not for a rejected certificate. Registry events omit thing type `propagatingAttributes` (not stored), publish no JOB `deletion_in_progress`/`cancellation_in_progress` (cancel and delete are synchronous) and no JOB_EXECUTION `removed`.

### Structural gaps

These do not block an A grade — no implementation could produce real data here because the underlying data source cannot exist in an emulator.

- ListMetricValues.DimensionName and DimensionValueOperator are not applied: no device reports metrics, datapoints are only seeded internally and carry no dimension.
- DeleteOTAUpdate.DeleteStream is not honored: CreateOTAUpdate never creates an OTA-owned stream (needs a real OTA stream pipeline); ForceDeleteAWSJob is honored.
- Device-fleet-dependent fields (no connection tracking): GetThingConnectivityData IncludeSocketInformation, Job IsConcurrent/ThingGroupId, TopicRuleDestination StatusReason.
- Rule actions timestream, kafka, location, openSearch, iotEvents, iotSiteWise, influxDB are stored verbatim but not executed (no data-plane backend); http enableBatching/batchConfig and errorAction cloudwatchTraceId/clientId are not modeled.
